blocks.text: 1. MobileNet

blocks.alt: MobileNet chains stacked separable conv blocks to an output

blocks.text: DenseNet, the previous topic, maximized feature reuse through dense connectivity. MobileNet is an architecture explicitly designed for resource-constrained, mobile deployment, a genuinely different design priority explored throughout this topic.
It is built almost entirely from Separable Convolution, already covered in its own topic, applying that efficient building block consistently throughout an entire network.
2. Recapping Separable Convolution

This connects back to Separable Convolution, already covered in the CNN module. Separable Convolution genuinely delivers dramatic parameter savings over ordinary convolution, already covered in complete detail there.
MobileNet genuinely builds an entire architecture around that single, efficient building block, using it as the genuinely primary, repeated unit throughout the entire network design.
3. Why Mobile Devices Genuinely Need This

blocks.alt: Mobile devices have limited compute and memory, which MobileNet fits

blocks.text: This connects back to the connection to mobile deployment, already covered in Depthwise Convolution. Phones and other genuinely resource-constrained devices have genuinely limited memory, compute, and battery life.

Ordinary convolutions, already covered, are often genuinely too expensive to run efficiently there, exactly the motivating problem that MobileNet's own design directly addresses throughout the rest of this topic.
4. Recapping The Building Block
This connects back to the full pipeline, already covered in Separable Convolution. Depthwise convolution filters each channel independently first, exactly the process already covered there.
Then a pointwise convolution mixes information across channels, exactly the sequence already covered, forming the exact repeated building block used consistently throughout MobileNet's entire design.

blocks.text: 5. The Width Multiplier

blocks.alt: The width multiplier reduces channels per layer

blocks.text: A genuinely important, tunable hyperparameter connects back to Hyperparameters, already covered in its own module. A width multiplier genuinely scales the number of channels throughout the entire network up or down.
This gives MobileNet a genuinely simple, direct knob for trading network capacity against computational cost, a genuinely practical tool for adapting to different deployment constraints.
6. The Resolution Multiplier

blocks.alt: The resolution multiplier gives a smaller input resolution

blocks.text: This connects back to Image Representation, already covered in its own topic. A genuinely separate resolution multiplier scales the input image's own size instead of the network's channel count.

Both knobs together, already covered in this topic, let MobileNet trade accuracy for genuinely further efficiency, giving practitioners genuinely fine-grained control over the network's own resource footprint.
7. The Accuracy-Efficiency Tradeoff

blocks.alt: High width and resolution is compared against low width and resolution

blocks.text: A genuinely honest, real tradeoff connects back to a genuine, honest tradeoff, already covered in Depthwise Convolution. Smaller width and resolution multipliers, already covered, genuinely reduce accuracy somewhat in exchange for genuinely more efficiency.

This is a genuinely real, practical tradeoff that every deployment decision using MobileNet must weigh carefully, balancing the specific device's own constraints against the task's own accuracy requirements.

blocks.title: warning
blocks.content: This accuracy-efficiency tradeoff, already covered in this topic, means there is genuinely no single best MobileNet configuration. The right width and resolution multipliers genuinely depend on the specific deployment target's own constraints.

blocks.text: 8. A Family Of Variants

blocks.alt: MobileNet has V1, V2, and V3 variants

blocks.text: A genuinely important, real practical detail connects back to VGG's own depth variants, already covered. MobileNet, like VGG, genuinely comes in a family of variants tuned for genuinely different efficiency targets.

This mirrors the same design pattern already covered in VGG, offering practitioners a genuinely practical range of choices along the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff already covered in the previous section.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When MobileNet Is Genuinely The Right Choice

blocks.alt: Needing on-device inference points toward using MobileNet

blocks.text: This connects forward to Production Deep Learning, covered later in this course, on genuinely constrained devices. MobileNet, already covered in this topic, is genuinely purpose built for exactly this deployment scenario.

Needing to tune the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff precisely for a specific device is another genuine case where the width and resolution multipliers, already covered, give genuinely direct, fine control over exactly that.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates how the width multiplier affects channel count and parameter count throughout a genuinely simplified MobileNet-style layer stack, illustrating the tradeoff already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
def separable_conv_params(filter_size, in_channels, out_channels):
    # already covered as the building block recap in this topic
    depthwise = filter_size * filter_size * in_channels
    pointwise = in_channels * out_channels
    return depthwise + pointwise

base_channels = [32, 64, 128, 256]  # a genuinely simplified channel progression

for width_multiplier in [1.0, 0.75, 0.5]:  # already covered as the width multiplier in this topic
    scaled_channels = [int(c * width_multiplier) for c in base_channels]
    total_params = sum(
        separable_conv_params(3, scaled_channels[i], scaled_channels[i + 1])
        for i in range(len(scaled_channels) - 1)
    )
    print(f"Width multiplier {width_multiplier}: channels {scaled_channels}, total params {total_params}")

print("\nSmaller width multipliers genuinely reduce both channel count and total parameters, already covered as the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff in this topic")

blocks.content: Running this example shows total parameters dropping substantially as the width multiplier decreases, exactly the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff already covered as this topic's own core practical mechanism.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: MobileNet is built almost entirely from Separable Convolution, designed for mobile deployment.
It addresses the real, practical memory, compute, and battery constraints of mobile devices.
Its building block is the same depthwise-then-pointwise sequence already covered in Separable Convolution.
A width multiplier scales the number of channels throughout the entire network.
A resolution multiplier scales the input image's own size instead.
Both knobs together let MobileNet trade accuracy for further efficiency, a real, honest tradeoff.
MobileNet comes in a family of variants, mirroring VGG's own tunable design pattern.
It is purpose built for resource-constrained, production deployment scenarios.
Next up: EfficientNet, an architecture that systematically studies how to scale networks optimally.
